Who we are

Two generations, one community

Building Bridges is a youth-led organization from Southborough and Northborough, Massachusetts. We connect local students with senior citizens so they can talk, play, learn from each other and give back to the towns they share.

Teens and senior citizens live on the same streets and shop at the same stores, but outside of family they rarely get to spend real time together. We're here to change that, one visit, one event and one conversation at a time.

Why it matters

Loneliness is a real health issue, and connection helps

Research shows that isolation takes a serious toll on older adults. It's also something a community can do something about.

1 in 4

Americans aged 65 and older living in the community are socially isolated.

National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, 2020. Read the report
43%

of adults aged 60 and older report feeling lonely.

National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, 2020.
15

A lack of social connection can be as harmful to health as smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day.

U.S. Surgeon General's advisory, 2023. Learn more

Building Bridges exists to make our corner of Massachusetts a little more connected.

About us

Bringing generations together, close to home

Who we are, what we believe and why we do it.

Our mission

Building Bridges connects young people and senior citizens in Southborough and Northborough through friendship, shared events and community service, so every generation in our towns feels seen, valued and connected.

Our vision

Two towns where every generation knows each other by name

We picture a community where a high schooler and a grandparent down the street can swap stories, trade skills and show up for each other.

Our story

Building Bridges was started by students from Southborough and Northborough who saw a gap in our community. Senior citizens have decades of stories, skills and wisdom to share. Students have energy, fresh ideas and plenty to learn. Outside of family, though, the two groups rarely cross paths.

So we decided to build a bridge between them. We organize events, lend a hand where it's needed and make room for real conversations between generations, right here in the towns we grew up in.

We're just getting started, and we'd love for you to be part of it.

What we believe

Our values

Connection

Real relationships that last longer than one afternoon. We come back, we remember names and we follow through.

Respect

Every person has a story worth hearing. We listen first and treat every neighbor with dignity.

Service

We show up for our community, whether that's running an event, spending time with senior citizens or lending a hand around town.

Fun

Bingo, games, good food and good company. Bringing people together should be a good time, and it is.

Our logo

Two people, one bridge

Look closely at our logo. It's two people standing on either side of a bridge: a taller figure in navy and a smaller one in gold, one older and one younger. Their arms reach toward each other and meet in the middle to form the arch.

That's the whole idea behind Building Bridges. A bridge only works when both sides reach out.

Navy stands for the steadiness that comes with experience. Gold stands for the energy young people bring.

What we do

Three ways we bring generations together

From big bingo afternoons to good conversation and community service, here's how Building Bridges works.

Events & get-togethers

Big, fun, all-ages gatherings where students and senior citizens spend time side by side. Our bingo and lunch with the senior center in March is next on the calendar.

  • Bingo afternoons and game days
  • Shared lunches and holiday get-togethers
  • Events planned with local senior centers

For senior citizens, students and families

See upcoming events

Conversation & connection

Sometimes the best thing we can do is sit down and talk. Senior citizens have amazing stories, and students have plenty to learn (and a few things to teach).

  • Conversation and card-game meetups
  • Swapping stories, skills and advice
  • Notes and handmade cards for the holidays

For anyone who'd enjoy some company

Community service

We pitch in around Southborough and Northborough wherever help is needed. A stronger community is better for every generation.

  • Helping set up and run community events
  • Seasonal service projects around town
  • Supply drives and other projects that support local senior citizens

About us

          
What is Building Bridges? 
Building Bridges is a student-run organization that connects young people and senior citizens in Southborough and Northborough, Massachusetts. We bring the two generations together through events, conversation and community service.

          
Who runs it? 
A leadership team of students, led by our two co-presidents, along with more than 20 student members from Southborough and Northborough. You can meet our leaders on the Team page.

          
Where are you located? 
We serve Southborough and Northborough, two neighboring towns in Worcester County, Massachusetts, between Worcester and Boston. Most of our activities happen at senior centers and other community spaces. See our location page for details.

          
Are you an official nonprofit? 
We're in the process of becoming one! Right now we're a student-run community group working on registering Building Bridges as an official nonprofit. We'll share an update here when it's done.

        

        

          
Volunteering

          
Who can volunteer? 
Students from Southborough, Northborough and nearby who want to spend time with senior citizens and help out in their community. If you're not sure you'd be a fit, reach out anyway.

          
Do I need any experience? 
Nope. Bring a good attitude and be ready to listen. We'll help with the rest.

          
How much time does it take? 
As much as you can give. You can help out at a single event or get involved in planning. Let us know what works for your schedule.

          
How do I sign up? 
Fill out the volunteer sign-up form and we'll get in touch.

        

        

          
Senior citizens & families

          
How can I take part as a senior citizen? 
Come to one of our events, or reach out if you'd just like some good conversation. You can also ask about us at your local senior center.

          
Can I sign up a parent or grandparent? 
Of course. Get in touch and tell us a little about them, and we'll help find a good fit.

          
Where do activities take place? 
Most of our activities happen at senior centers and other public community spaces in Southborough and Northborough.

        

        

          
Donations & partners

          
How will my donation be used? 
All proceeds from our online fundraiser go to two places: senior citizens with disabilities living in assisted living, and the Southborough and Northborough Senior Centers. Supplies you donate go toward our events. See our Donate page for more.

          
Is my donation tax-deductible? 
Not yet. We're still in the process of becoming an official nonprofit, so donations aren't tax-deductible right now. We'll update this page when that changes.

          
Can I donate supplies instead of money? 
Absolutely. Check our wish list for the things we use most.

          
How can my business partner with you? 
Sponsor an event, donate food or prizes, host us or help spread the word. Visit our Partners page to learn more.

        

        

          
Still have a question?
We're happy to help.
